title: mandate (SPEC 3.2 + 17.2): the principal's limits as code
description: SPEC 3.2 with the fields section 17 adds: expires_at, scope.counterparties, scope.purpose_codes, scope.step_up_above_minor, scope.unattended, principal_sig. Fields are only added (SPEC 8): verifyMandate keeps working on these objects. The free-text purpose stays for people and is never evaluated by a gate; the gate reads purpose_codes.

how.description: How the principal confirmed the limits.

counterparties.description: Agent ids the agent may pay. ["*"] is the principal's explicit choice to allow any; an empty list is not allowed.

purpose_codes.description: The purpose as code, matched against the deal's purpose_code. No free text is ever evaluated.

step_up_above_minor.description: Above this amount every transfer needs a step_up object; null: never.

unattended.description: May the agent spend with no human present? false: every transfer is a step-up unless the request says human_present.

purpose.description: A sentence for people, no personal data. Never evaluated by a gate.

expires_at.description: Required by the gate (MANDATE_NO_EXPIRY). An ended mandate is a mandate_end statement, as in SPEC 3.2.

principal_sig.description: Optional: the principal's own Ed25519 signature over canonical(mandate without sig and principal_sig). This makes the mandate a verifiable intent in the sense of AP2: the issuer saw it, and the principal signed it.
